pandas.to_datetime

pandas 3.1.1 · General functions · function

Parse input as datetimes. Use format for a known layout, utc=True to normalize to UTC and errors="coerce" to mark invalid values as NaT.

  • Call syntax
  • Run the example

Call syntax

pd.to_datetime(…) Full signature
pd.to_datetime(
    arg,
    errors='raise',
    dayfirst=False,
    yearfirst=False,
    utc=False,
    format=None,
    exact=…,
    unit=None,
    origin='unix',
    cache=True,
)

Parameters
ParameterRequirementAccepted values and behavior
arg
      Required
Positional or keyword		
      int, float, str, datetime, list, tuple, 1-d array, Series, DataFrame/dict-like
Pass date text, a numeric epoch value, a datetime, an array-like, or a table with date fields.


errors
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default 'raise'		
      {'raise', 'coerce'}
Choose "raise" to reject invalid dates or "coerce" to turn them into NaT.


dayfirst
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default False		
      bool
Prefer the day before the month when interpreting ambiguous date text.


yearfirst
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default False		
      bool


utc
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default False		
      bool
True localizes naive values to UTC and converts timezone-aware values to UTC.


format
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default None		
      str
Use a strftime-style pattern for a known layout, "ISO8601" for ISO text, or "mixed" to infer per value.


exact
      Optional
Positional or keyword		
      bool
Choose whether the parser requires an exact format match.


unit
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default None		
      str
Specify the time unit represented by each number or required by the result.


origin
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default 'unix'		
      scalar
Choose the reference timestamp or origin from which a numeric time or bin is measured.


cache
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default True		
      bool
Reuse the conversion of repeated date strings where pandas can apply the cache.
